title: एनटीएको सूचनाले फेरि गिजोलियो टीएससी विवाद, आईएसपीको मर्मत सम्भार शुल्कमा छेडखानीको आशंका

No ads found for this position नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकलाई १० दिनभित्र दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुरसम्बन्धी विवरण बुझाउन भनेको छ, जसको विरोधमा सेवा प्रदायकहरूले आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले मर्मतसम्भारका नाममा वास्तविक खर्चभन्दा बढी शुल्क उठाउँदै आएको र यसले नेपाल सरकारलाई राजस्व हानी नोक्सानी गरिरहेको आरोप लागेको छ। प्राधिकरणले टीएससीको अनियमितता र मर्मतसम्भार खर्चको वास्तविकतालाई ध्यानमा राखेर उचित कदम चाल्नुपर्ने आवश्यकता व्यक्त गरिएको छ। The Nepal Telecommunications Authority has asked internet service providers to submit details of telecommunication service charges within 10 days, to which service providers have objected. Internet service providers have been charging more than the actual costs in the name of maintenance, and this has been causing revenue loss to the Nepal government. The need has been expressed for the authority to take appropriate steps, keeping in mind the irregularities and the reality of maintenance expenses of TSC. काठमाडौं । दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तूरसम्बन्धी विवरण १० दिनभित्र बुझाउनु भनी नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले जारी गरेको सूचना आफैंमा विवादमा परेको छ । एकातिर इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकले त्यसको नियतमाथि आपत्ति जनाएका छन् भने अर्कोतर्फ यही सूचनाको आडमा अर्बौं राजश्व हानी नोक्सानी पार्न खोजिएको आशंका पनि व्यक्त भएको छ । नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले गत मंसिर २ गते दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुरसँग सम्बन्धित आवश्यक कागजातहरूसहित १० दिनभित्र विवरण पेस गर्न सबै इन्टरनेट (इमेलसहित) सेवा प्रदायकका नाममा सार्वजनिक सूचना निकालेको थियो । जारी सूचनामा आर्थिक ऐन, २०८३ को दफा ८ को उपदफा ५ मा “दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुरको प्रशासन नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले निर्धारण गरेबमोजिम हुनेछ” भन्ने व्यवस्था रहेको उल्लेख छ। सोहीअनुसार प्राधिकरणबाट दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालन गर्न अनुमतिपत्र प्राप्त गरी सेवा सञ्चालन गरिरहेका सेवा प्रदायकहरूले आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ र चालू आर्थिक वर्षको असोज महिनासम्म नियमानुसार नेपाल सरकारको राजस्व खातामा दाखिला गरेको टीएससी विवरणसँग सम्बन्धी कागजात बुझाउन भनिएको थियो । प्राधिकरणले जारी गरेको उक्त सूचनामा इन्टरनेट (इमेलसहित) सेवा प्रदायकलाई मात्र लक्षित गरिएकोमा इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले भने आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। आर्थिक ऐनले आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि नै दूरसञ्चार सेवा शुल्कमा दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (Telecommunication Service Charge: टीएससी) लगाउँदै आएको र हाल नेपालमा विभिन्न प्रकारका दूरसञ्चार सेवा सञ्चालनमा रहे पनि इन्टरनेट (इमेलसहित) सेवा प्रदायकलाई मात्र लक्षित गरी सूचना प्रकाशन गर्दा प्राधिकरणले कानुनी व्यवस्थाको हेक्का नराखेको तथा एउटा मात्र प्रकारको सेवा प्रदायकप्रति आमजनमानसमा नकारात्मक सन्देश प्रवाह गर्न खोजिएको उनीहरूको गुनासो छ । प्राधिकरणले मासिक रूपमा टीएससी जम्मा गरेको विवरण मागेको छ । दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, सोही नियमावली, २०५४ र आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखिका आर्थिक ऐनहरूले समग्रतामा गरेको व्यवस्थाबमोजिम फिक्स्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवामा (कुनै कारणले दूरसञ्चार सेवा बिग्रिएमा मर्मतसम्भार गर्नुपर्दा सेवा प्रदायकको जतिसुकै खर्च अर्थात् Cost of Support and Maintenance लागे पनि) उपभोक्ताबाट लिने मासिक महसुलको अधिकतम ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको रकम मात्र मर्मतसम्भारबापत लिन पाउने र उक्त रकममा टीएससी नलाग्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था रहेको छ। यसरी इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले मर्मतसम्भारको नाममा गरेको वास्तविक खर्च ( Actual Cost of Support and Maintenance ) मा मात्र टीएससी नलाग्ने स्वतः स्पष्ट छ। तर, अधिकांश इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले वार्षिक रूपमा गरेको यस्तो मर्मतसम्भार खर्च उनीहरूको वार्षिक आम्दानीको ५ प्रतिशतभन्दा पनि न्यून रहेको देखिन्छ । त्यस्तो अवस्थामा पनि उनीहरूले हाल इन्टरनेट वा दूरसञ्चार सेवाका उपभोक्तालाई बिलिङ गर्दा इन्टरनेट सेवा शुल्कको १०० प्रतिशत बराबरको रकम मर्मतसम्भारका रूपमा उठाएको देखाएका छन्। यस कार्यले नेपाल सरकारलाई प्राप्त हुनुपर्ने टीएससीको आधार मूल्यलाई घटाउने, हटाउने, नास्ने, मास्ने वा कम देखाउने गरी नियतवश राजस्व हानीनोक्सानी गरिएको भनी इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूमाथि ठूला करदाता कार्यालयले गरेको छानबिन तथा अनुसन्धानबाट समेत नेपाल सरकारले टीएससी र जरिवानाबापत अर्बौं रूपैयाँ प्राप्त गर्ने अवस्था सिर्जना भएको छ । हाल नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूबाट मासिक विवरण माग गरेको सन्दर्भमा केही इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको वार्षिक अडिट रिपोर्टसमेतका आधारमा नेपााल प्रेस को विज्ञ टोलीले अध्ययन गर्दा असूल हुनुपर्ने टीएससी र सोको जरिवानाबापतको अनुमानित रकमको हिसाबकिताब देहायबमोजिम देखिएको छ- भायानेट कम्युनिकेसन्स (Vianet Communications): भायानेट कम्युनिकेसन्सबाट आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखि आर्थिक वर्ष २०८१/८२ सम्मको अवधिमा नेपाल सरकारलाई प्राप्त हुनुपर्ने टीएससी तथा सोको जरिवानाबापतको रकम १ अर्ब ७७ करोड रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी देखिएको छ। यस हिसाबमा इन्टरनेट सेवाबापतको आम्दानी मात्र देखाइएकाले सो कम्पनीले प्राप्त गरेको अनुमतिपत्रअन्तर्गत टीएससीयोग्य अन्य आम्दानीसमेत हिसाब गर्ने हो भने यो रकम अझै बढ्न सक्ने देखिएको छ। Note: TSC योग्य सम्पूर्ण आम्दानीको हिसाब गर्दा Vianet ले TSC मा भएको हानी नोक्सानी तथा प्रत्येक महिना को ५% को दरले जरिवाना समेत गरी हुन आउने रकमको आधारमा TSC मा भएको हानी नोक्सानी रकम रू. ७२,५५,४२,३८१/- र सो को जरिवाना २,२४,२५,३१,१३१/- समेत गरी हुन आउने रकम रू. २,९६,८०,७३,५१३ /- (२ अर्व, ९६ करोड, ८० लाख, ७३ हजार, ५१२/-) बुझाउनु पर्ने देखिन्छ। सुबिसु (SuBiSu Cablenet) आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागबाट गरिएको अनुसन्धान समेतको आधारमा सुबिसुले TSC मा भएको हानी नोक्सानी तथा सो बापतको जरिवाना समेत बुझाउनु पर्ने रकमको विवरण- टेकमाइन्ड्स (Techminds): टीएससीयोग्य सम्पूर्ण आम्दानीको हिसाब गर्दा टेकमाइन्ड्सले टीएससीमा पुर्‍याएको हानिनोक्सानी रकम रु. २५,१५,३३,५८२.६० र मासिक ५ प्रतिशतका दरले लाग्ने जरिवाना रु. ५८,४८,१५,८२५/- समेत गरी कुल रु. ८३,६३,४९,४०८/- (८३ करोड ६३ लाख ४९ हजार ४०८ रुपैयाँ) बुझाउनुपर्ने देखिन्छ। क्लासिक टेक (Classic Tech): टीएससीयोग्य सम्पूर्ण आम्दानीको हिसाब गर्दा क्लासिक टेकले टीएससीमा पुर्‍याएको हानिनोक्सानी रकम रु. २०,४०,४७,०५५/- र मासिक ५ प्रतिशतका दरले लाग्ने जरिवाना रु. ६०,१७,२४,२४६/- समेत गरी कुल रु. ८०,५७,७१,३०१/- (८० करोड ५७ लाख ७१ हजार ३०१ रुपैयाँ) बुझाउनुपर्ने देखिन्छ। छेडखानीको आशंका नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले जारी गरेको सूचनामा मर्मतसम्भारबापतको आय खुलाउन भनिएको छ, तर मर्मतसम्भारबापतको वास्तविक खर्च ( Actual Cost of Support and Maintenance ) भने खुलाउन नभनिएकाले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले स्वघोषणा गरेको मर्मतसम्भारबापतको आयमा नै टीएससी छुट दिई अनियमितता गर्न खोजिएको विज्ञहरूले बताएका छन् । हाल इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूले इन्टरनेट सेवाबापतको आम्दानीकै बराबर हुने गरी १०० प्रतिशत मर्मतसम्भारबापत शुल्क उठाउँदै आएका छन् । तर, वास्तविक रूपमा मर्मतसम्भारमा करिब ४ देखि ७ प्रतिशतसम्म मात्र खर्च हुने गरेको पाइएको छ । यसरी सरकारलाई प्राप्त हुने टीएससीको आधार शुल्कलाई कृत्रिम रूपमा घटाई सरकारी राजस्वमा हानिनोक्सानी पुर्‍याएको विषयमा आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागले गरेको अनुसन्धानबाट स्थापित रकम असुलउपर गर्न नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले देखाएको उदासीनताले थप आशङ्का जन्माएको छ । आर्थिक ऐनले वास्तविक रूपमा भएको मर्मतसम्भार खर्चमा मात्र टीएससी छुट दिएको जगजाहेर रहँदा पनि इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक (आईएसपी) हरूले स्वघोषणा गरेको इन्टरनेट शुल्कको १०० प्रतिशत बराबरको मर्मतसम्भार शुल्कमा टीएससी छुट दिई नेपाल सरकारलाई हानिनोक्सानी पुर्‍याउन खोजिएको आशङ्का गरिएको छ। Kathmandu. The notice issued by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority asking for details of telecommunications service charges to be submitted within 10 days has itself been mired in controversy. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers . However, it appears that the annual maintenance expenditure incurred by most Internet service providers is less than 5 percent of their annual revenue. Even in such a situation, they have shown that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance while billing consumers of Internet or telecommunication services. This act has created a situation where the Government of Nepal has received billions of rupees in TSC and fines through the investigation and investigation conducted by the Big Taxpayers Office on Internet service providers, which has deliberately caused revenue loss by reducing, removing, destroying, destroying or understating the base value of TSC that should have been received by the Government of Nepal. In the context of the Nepal Telecommunication Authority currently requesting monthly statements from Internet service providers, based on the annual audit reports of some Internet service providers, a team of experts from Nepal Press has studied the estimated amount of TSC and fines to be collected as follows: Vianet Communications: The amount of TSC and fines due to the Government of Nepal from Vianet Communications for the period from fiscal year 2075/76 to fiscal year 2081/82 is more than 1.77 billion rupees. Since this calculation shows only income from internet services, it is likely that this amount will increase further if other income eligible for TSC under the license obtained by the company is also calculated. Note: When calculating the total TSC eligible income, Vianet will have to pay the TSC loss and damage amount of Rs. 72,55,42,381/- and the fine of Rs. 2,24,25,31,131/-, which is Rs. 2,96,80,73,513/- (2,960,000,800,73,512/-) based on the amount that will be incurred including the loss and damage to TSC and the penalty at the rate of 5% per month. SuBiSu Cablenet Based on the investigation conducted by the Department of Internal Revenue, Subisu has provided details of the amount of damages and fines that TSC has to pay: Techminds: When calculating the total income eligible for TSC, it appears that TechMinds has to pay a total of Rs. 83,63,49,408/- (836,349,408 rupees) including the loss and damage amount incurred by TSC of Rs. 25,15,33,582.60 and a penalty of Rs. 58,48,15,825/- at the rate of 5 percent per month. Classic Tech: When calculating the total income eligible for TSC, it appears that Classic Tech has to pay a total of Rs. 80,57,71,301/- (800 million 57 lakh 71 thousand 301 rupees) including the loss and damage amount incurred by TSC at Rs. 20,40,47,055/- and a penalty of Rs. 60,17,24,246/- at the rate of 5 percent per month. Suspicion of molestation Experts have said that since the notice issued by the Nepal Telecommunication Authority asks for the disclosure of maintenance income, but does not ask for the disclosure of the actual cost of support and maintenance, an attempt is being made to commit irregularities by granting TSC exemption on the maintenance income declared by the internet service providers. Currently, Internet service providers are charging 100 percent maintenance fees, which is equal to the revenue from Internet services. However, it has been found that in reality, only about 4 to 7 percent is spent on maintenance. The Nepal Telecommunication Authority's indifference to recover the amount established by the Department of Internal Revenue's investigation into the artificially reduced base fee of TSC received by the government, causing loss to government revenue, has raised further suspicions. Despite the fact that the Finance Act provides TSC exemption only for actual maintenance expenses incurred, there is suspicion that Internet Service Providers (ISPs) are attempting to cause harm to the Government of Nepal by granting TSC exemption on maintenance fees equal to 100 percent of the self-declared internet fees.

The notice issued by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority asking for details of telecommunications service charges to be submitted within 10 days has itself been mired in controversy. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers . However, it appears that the annual maintenance expenditure incurred by most Internet service providers is less than 5 percent of their annual revenue. Even in such a situation, they have shown that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance while billing consumers of Internet or telecommunication services. The notice issued by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority asking for details of telecommunications service charges to be submitted within 10 days has itself been mired in controversy. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers . However, it appears that the annual maintenance expenditure incurred by most Internet service providers is less than 5 percent of their annual revenue. Even in such a situation, they have shown that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance while billing consumers of Internet or telecommunication services. The notice issued by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority asking for details of telecommunications service charges to be submitted within 10 days has itself been mired in controversy. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers . However, it appears that the annual maintenance expenditure incurred by most Internet service providers is less than 5 percent of their annual revenue. Even in such a situation, they have shown that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance while billing consumers of Internet or telecommunication services. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers . However, it appears that the annual maintenance expenditure incurred by most Internet service providers is less than 5 percent of their annual revenue. Even in such a situation, they have shown that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance while billing consumers of Internet or telecommunication services. On the one hand, internet service providers have objected to its intentions, while on the other hand, suspicions have been expressed that billions of rupees in revenue loss have been caused under the guise of this information. On November 20, the Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) issued a public notice to all internet (including email) service providers to submit details related to telecommunication service charges within 10 days along with necessary documents. The notice issued states that “the administration of telecommunications service charges shall be as determined by the Nepal Telecommunications Authority” in Section 8, Sub-Section 5 of the Finance Act, 2083. Accordingly, service providers who have obtained a license to operate telecommunications services from the authority and are operating the service were asked to submit documents related to the TSC details submitted to the revenue account of the Government of Nepal as per the rules for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year by the month of Ashoj. Internet service providers have objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers. The Finance Act has been imposing a Telecommunication Service Charge (TSC) on telecommunications service fees since the fiscal year 2075/76, and although various types of telecommunications services are currently operating in Nepal, the Authority has not taken into account the legal provisions while publishing the notice targeting only Internet (including email) service providers and is trying to send a negative message to the general public towards only one type of service provider. The Authority has requested details of monthly TSC collection. As per the provisions of the Telecommunications Act, 2053, the same Regulations, 2054, and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76, in fixed broadband services (regardless of the cost of support and maintenance incurred by the service provider if the telecommunications service is damaged for any reason ), only a maximum of 50 percent of the monthly fee collected from the consumer can be collected for maintenance and there is a legal provision that TSC will not be levied on that amount. Thus, it is self-evident that TSC is not levied on the actual cost of support and maintenance incurred by Internet service providers .
